clue.text: Perusing change, daydream ultimately internalised by comic character

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word it follows, so only its final letter is kept
something internalised is taken inside, so the earlier pieces sit within the word that follows

blocks.note: to change something is to alter it
the last letter of daydream
comic and witty both mean funny

explanation.surface: Someone reading about change while a daydream gets absorbed into a funny figure from the comics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the outer word that swallows the rest. 'Perusing' adds nothing to the wordplay and serves only the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Mitty is James Thurber's fictional daydreamer, a famous literary figure whose name now labels any fantasist.

clue.text: Rich, healthy stew

blocks.note: being well means being in good health
a stew or a to-do is a state of agitated fuss

explanation.surface: A hearty, nourishing stew described as rich and wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like food but means a fuss, as in 'getting into a stew'.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do describes people who are prosperous and comfortably off, a standard synonym for wealthy.

clue.text: The French politician to put online support for Enlightenment

blocks.note: la is French for the (feminine)
Member of Parliament
to post something is to put it up on the internet

explanation.surface: A French politician posting online in favour of Enlightenment philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enlightenment' suggests the 18th-century movement, but it is meant literally: the support holds up a light.
explanation.definitionFit: A street lamp sits on top of a tall post, which physically holds the light up, playfully described as supporting illumination.

clue.text: Wear down the Queen with dedicatory verse

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
an ode is a lyric poem often addressed to someone

explanation.surface: Tiring out the monarch by presenting her with a poem in her honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water and wind do to rock.

clue.text: Confused mediator ignoring old hotel employee

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up and put back in a different order
ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A bewildered go-between who pays no attention to some elderly worker at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A maître d' is the head waiter who runs a hotel or restaurant dining room and greets guests.

clue.text: Walk unsteadily with end of skewer stuck in foot

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept
something stuck in another thing is lodged inside it

blocks.note: to totter is to walk in a wobbly way
the final letter of skewer

explanation.surface: Someone limping along after stabbing their foot on the end of a kebab skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is the foot of a pig, sold as a cut of meat, so the word names an animal's foot.

clue.text: ‘Much beer ordered for lad?’ ‘Aye’

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged, so the letters are put into a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barroom exchange: someone asks if a big drink was ordered for the lad, and the reply is yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as placing a drinks order, but it rearranges the letters of 'for lad' and 'Aye'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is a very tall glass holding about two and a half pints, a large quantity of beer.

clue.text: Where a slope is regularly seen?

definitions.text: Where a slope is regularly seen?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of these words

explanation.surface: A riddle asking where you would routinely spot a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: mountain slopes are a common sight in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, especially in Switzerland, a place known for steep ski slopes.

clue.text: Inseam tailored in city near Lille

indicators.note: tailored material is cut and refashioned, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Trouser seams altered by a tailor in a northern French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a cathedral city in Picardy, northern France, not far south of Lille.

clue.text: A sleep, for a change – I'd like that

indicators.note: for a change suggests doing something differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fancying a nap as a welcome break from routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'please' accepts an offer politely, which expresses that you would welcome it.

clue.text: Bishop in fancy car, finding borderland of Hell

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

blocks.note: a limo is a luxurious car
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop riding in a flashy limousine and discovering the edge of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic theology limbo is the region on the edge of Hell for souls not damned but excluded from heaven.

clue.text: Routine I’m rewriting for Radio 4 show

indicators.note: rewriting reworks text, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A scriptwriter reworking a sketch for broadcast on BBC radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio 4 is the BBC's speech station; In Our Time is its long-running discussion programme presented by Melvyn Bragg.
explanation.definitionFit: In Our Time is a well-known programme broadcast on that BBC network, so it is an example of a show there.

clue.text: Violent protest about von der Leyen etc being privileged

indicators.note: something violent is disrupted and thrown about, so these letters are scrambled
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: taken as written
Ursula von der Leyen heads the European Commission, abbreviated EC

explanation.surface: Angry demonstrations against Ursula von der Leyen and her colleagues for being an elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'von der Leyen etc' is the body she and her fellow commissioners form: the European Commission.
explanation.definitionFit: Privileged information is confidential and restricted, so highly classified material counts as privileged.

clue.text: ‘Noise of geese not hard,’ Everyman accepted, producing noise of pigs

indicators.note: not here tells us a letter is to be left out
something accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: geese honk
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
the setter refers to himself, so Everyman gives I

explanation.surface: A farmyard comedy where the setter's geese start squealing like pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinks are the grunting sounds pigs make, an imitative word for porcine noise.

clue.text: Yearned for title, ‘knight’ included

indicators.note: included means put within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a title deed proves ownership of property
a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: Someone longing for an honour, with a knighthood thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' suggests a rank like Sir, but here it is the legal document of ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired means wanted or longed for, the same as yearned for, both past participles.

clue.text: Number one coming down to 20?

blocks.note: first meaning: a song, Elton John's 1972 hit
second meaning: an astronaut descending for 20-down, the return to the atmosphere

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' suggests a chart topper, but 'Number' and 'one' belong to separate definitions. 20 is the cross-reference to 20-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket Man is a well-known Elton John song, and literally a spaceman who rides a rocket home through the atmosphere.

clue.text: ‘Sincere’ earl corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled and altered from its proper form, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman who seemed honest turns out to have been bribed.
explanation.definitionFit: Real feelings are genuine and heartfelt, so the adjective is a synonym for sincere.

clue.text: Soundly thrashed, English batsman visibly embarrassed

indicators.note: soundly here means going by sound, so the word is spelt as it is pronounced

blocks.note: thrashed means beaten
Joe Root is a leading English Test cricketer

explanation.surface: An England cricketer left red-faced after a heavy defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly thrashed' reads as 'heavily beaten', but 'Soundly' flags a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In British idiom someone who goes beetroot blushes deep red, the colour of the vegetable.

clue.text: Dickens’ protagonist entered into dreary monotonous labour

indicators.note: a thing entered into goes inside another

blocks.note: dry can mean dull and uninteresting
Barnaby Rudge is the title hero of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A Dickensian hero trapped in grim, tedious toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, menial, repetitive work, the kind that is dull and wearisome.

clue.text: Ignore extremes in Holy Land's measure

indicators.note: extremes are the first and last letters, which we are told to disregard

blocks.note: holy and sacred are synonyms

explanation.surface: A measurement made in the Holy Land, leaving out the far ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre is also a port city in Israel, which makes 'Holy Land' look like the definition; the definition is 'Land's measure'.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit for measuring area of ground, 4,840 square yards.

clue.text: Hearing indication you’re being talked about!

blocks.note: first meaning: within range of hearing
second meaning, split as two words: burning ears are said to show that others are gossiping about you

explanation.walkthrough: The folk belief is that your ears burn when someone is discussing you; read the answer as two words for the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which a sound can be heard, so a sense of hearing range.

clue.text: Cockney’s come to us on a horse, they say (it’s another animal)

indicators.note: they say points to what people speak, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.clueFragment: Cockney’s come to us on a horse
blocks.note: rode here, with the Cockney dropping the h

explanation.surface: A Londoner arriving on horseback, followed by a wry aside that we are dealing with yet another beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, traditionally drop the h, so 'rode here' becomes 'rode 'ere'.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European deer species, a creature other than the horse already in the clue.

clue.text: Perhaps rocket wanting gravity to attempt return to atmosphere

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

blocks.note: rocket is a salad leaf, an example of greens
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: A spacecraft without gravity trying to come back into the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' sits in a space scene, but it is the leafy salad vegetable known in the US as arugula.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry is the stage when a spacecraft comes back into Earth's atmosphere from space.

clue.text: With essential ingredient missing, recipes made dodgy French food

indicators.note: the essential part is the heart of the word, which is absent
making something dodgy means messing it up, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written; its central letter is removed

explanation.surface: A cook leaves out a key ingredient and botches some French dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crêpes are thin French pancakes, a classic dish of that country's cuisine.

clue.text: Puritan zealously rejected a root crop

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so a letter is removed
zealously suggests frantic energy that throws the letters into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strict Puritan fervently refusing to eat a humble vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a vegetable grown for its swollen edible root, a classic field crop.

clue.text: Don’t just throw away waste, avoiding fine

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: refuse is rubbish
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Recycling advice: don't throw rubbish out, and you won't get fined.
explanation.definitionFit: To reuse something is to use it again, the alternative to discarding it after one use.

clue.text: Staggered around drunkenly, etc, and returned to office

indicators.note: something done drunkenly is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to reel is to stagger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician who lurched about drunk and so on, yet still won back their seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being re-elected means winning another term, being voted back into the same position.

clue.text: King Ethelred garrotted (to some extent)

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so just a portion of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king partly strangled.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred looks like the king, but the king is concealed within the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar was a tenth-century English king, father of Ethelred the Unready.

clue.text: Both parents touring North Australia, energy fading in heat, getting protection from sun

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the outer pieces surround the inner one
fading means disappearing, so a letter vanishes from the following word

blocks.note: father and mother, PA and MA
N for north and A for Australia
E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad on a trip round the Northern Territory, wilting in the heat and needing shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama hat is a lightweight straw hat with a brim, worn to shade the head in hot weather.

clue.text: Run into Brexiteer in wood

indicators.note: into means going inside another thing

blocks.note: Michael Gove was a leading Brexit campaigner
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into a Leave campaigner while walking in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove is a British Conservative politician who campaigned for Brexit in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small wood or group of trees, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Step back, idiot

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a pas is a step in ballet

explanation.surface: Telling a fool to move out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step back' reads as a command, but it is the ballet step written in the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sap is a gullible, foolish person, an informal synonym for a simpleton.

clue.text: Lousy granular brass tacks

blocks.note: lousy literally means infested with lice, whose eggs are nits
gritty means made of small grains

explanation.surface: Something dreadful and grainy, described as basic facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' looks like 'bad', but is meant literally: full of lice and their nits.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the nitty-gritty or brass tacks both mean dealing with the essential basic facts of a matter.
